label: ESTIMATED pressure / relative 0-100
description: An explicitly heuristic simulation from visually reviewed right-camera contact phases and original right-hand joint bends. The right hand steadies a glass cup by its handle, lifts and carries it, places it in the microwave, then releases. Contact strengths and pad locations are assumptions, not recovered forces or measured pressure.

video_observations.observation: Gloved right hand approaches/closes around the cup handle on the table.
Left hand starts pouring from a kettle while the right hand steadies the cup handle.
Pouring ends; the cup remains near the table in the right grip.
The filled cup is visibly lifted and moved away from the table.
Right hand carries the cup by its handle. Left hand briefly supports/touches the cup.
Left hand opens the microwave; right hand keeps carrying the cup.
Right hand lowers the cup onto the microwave turntable; fingers are partly occluded.
Cup is resting inside; gloved right hand begins withdrawing from the handle.
Right hand withdraws and opens; exact contact end is approximate.
Open right hand is away from the cup and visibly unloaded.

assumptions: Relative intensity rises during lift/carry and falls when the table/turntable supports the cup. No object mass, friction, force, contact area or kPa is estimated.
Thumb/index/middle dominate handle contact; ring/little and palm receive small assumed loads. Occluded pad contacts cannot be resolved from video.
Original distal joint bends modulate contact amplitudes by 0.65 + 0.35 * normalized curl; finger bending without annotated contact produces zero pressure.
Missing/degenerate raw pose uses only the interpolated visual contact envelope and an explicit neutral curl prior of 0.55. It is labeled VIDEO ONLY and never written into pose/flexion.
Keyframe strengths use smoothstep interpolation. Contact timing is visually annotated and approximate (~0.2 s at release), not sensor timing.
The open-hand atlas is intentionally fixed to compare regions; the separate flexion panel shows the recorded pose.
